notes: Imported 24 exercises, ids 4801-4824, spread over grades 8 to 12 and difficulties 2 to 5. Worked sessions 5, 6, 8 (Group A: apportionment, voting power, Math Relays) and the two 2007 named talks, handoutId10-0.pdf (Introduction to Induction, Olga Radko) and handoutId11-0.pdf (Essential Counting Strategies, Kevin Wang). THREE SAME-FOLDER DUPLICATES with another agent's block, all from the induction material: 4801 = 2005 (Tous les chevaux ont la meme couleur), 4805 = 2006 (two-colouring the plane cut by lines), 4806 = 2004 (Fibonacci identity F(n-1)F(n+1) - F(n)^2). The other agent worked Handout-991-1043.pdf (Advanced, Induction I), which carries the same classics as Olga Radko's 2007 talk. Per the parallel-import rule nothing was deleted; the coordinator should keep one of each pair. LESSON FOR THE NEXT PASS: the 2007-2008 named talks overlap heavily with the Advanced induction and counting handouts, so run 'vm.py list --grade 11' and '--grade 12' before writing anything from them. Sessions 0-4 and 7 are dead ends, see skipped. Resume at session 9 (Problems with Trees / Combinatorial Game Theory, which has an answers file).

verified_answers.q: 10 seats, crews 77/46/30/27, four apportionment methods
verified_answers.a: Hamilton (largest remainder) 4-3-2-1 ; Jefferson (round down, lower D, e.g. D=15,2) 5-3-1-1 ; Adams (round up, raise D, e.g. D=23) 4-2-2-2 ; Webster (round to nearest, e.g. D=18,2) 4-3-2-1

verified_answers.q: Emerald City council, weights 5, 3, 1, 1, 1, quota 8
verified_answers.a: 9 winning coalitions, powers 9/19, 7/19, 1/19, 1/19, 1/19 (brute forced). Nice surprise: Dorothy with 3 votes outweighs the three 1-vote members put together.

verified_answers.q: 'prime-looking' numbers below 1000 (composite, not divisible by 2, 3 or 5)
number of possible endpoints of a ten-step lattice walk
verified_answers.a: 121 (brute forced); the reachable points are |x|+|y| <= 10 with |x|+|y| even

verified_answers.q: bug on a cube, 7 random moves, visits every vertex exactly once
verified_answers.a: 18 Hamiltonian paths from a fixed vertex, probability 18/3^7 = 2/243 (brute forced)

verified_answers.q: subsets of {1..15}, no two consecutive, min element >= size
squares with all four vertices in a 10x10 array of points (tilted ones included)
the inequality printed as '2^n > 1 + n 2^(n-1)'
verified_answers.a: the real statement is 2^n > 1 + n*sqrt(2^(n-1)) for n >= 2; the flat text drops the square root sign

verified_answers.q: the divisibility printed as '2^3n + 1 divisible by 3^(n+1)'
verified_answers.a: the real statement is 2^(3^n) + 1, a nested power. The flat reading 2^(3n) is false already at n = 2 (65 is not divisible by 27). Imported as 4802.
